description: Conformance vectors for the did:webvh witness rail (identity-did.md §3.4.1-§3.4.3). Two layers are exercised and MUST NOT be conflated. cryptographic_vectors[] contains a field-exact, externally sourced did:webvh v1.0 log and did-witness.json whose entry hash, controller proof and witness proof MUST all be recomputed and verified. method_policy_cases[] cover structural and policy semantics: witness policy is read only from parameters.witness = {threshold, witnesses:[{id}]} whose ids are did:key values that MUST decode to cryptosuite-compatible public keys during parameter validation, proofs come only from the separate did-witness.json keyed by versionId, and every malformed, aliased, unavailable or under-threshold condition fails closed with a registered code instead of degrading to threshold 0. schema_validation_cases[] cover the Arkret-layer carrier: ak.schema.did_webvh_witness_receipt.v1 is a distinct object family from ak.schema.identity_receipt.v1 and the two are returned as a tagged union discriminated on schema. The receipt is a cacheable, auditable observation record; it never substitutes for verifying the standard did-witness.json proofs, the entry hash chain or the controller proof. Placeholder values occur only in the explicitly structural cases; they MUST NOT be substituted for cryptographic_vectors[].

method_policy_cases.name: standard_witness_parameter_is_the_only_policy_source
method_policy_cases.notes: The did:webvh 1.0 shape. threshold is within 1..witnesses.length and every witness id is a unique did:key. This is the only structure an Arkret verifier reads as witness policy.

method_policy_cases.name: absent_witness_parameter_means_no_method_witness
method_policy_cases.notes: Absence is not malformation. A DID that never declared method witnesses is legitimately unwitnessed at the method layer; deployment policy may still refuse to use it on high-risk paths, but that is an overlay decision and not a parse failure.

method_policy_cases.name: aliased_witness_keys_fail_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: The single most dangerous case. A log carrying witnesses / witness_threshold instead of witness was produced against a non-standard dialect, so the true policy is unknown. Reading it as no policy would silently turn a DID that declares two witnesses into one that requires none, which is a fail-open, not a compatibility fallback.

method_policy_cases.name: arkret_overlay_fields_inside_method_parameter_fail_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: profileMinThreshold / structuredWitnesses / watcherEvidence / maxAgeSeconds are Arkret deployment policy. Inside method history they force external verifiers to cope with unregistered keys, make policy rotation require rewriting DID history, and let a holder self-declare both the threshold and the evidence that satisfies it.

method_policy_cases.name: non_did_key_witness_id_fails_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: did:webvh 1.0 constrains witness identifiers to did:key. Any other form describes something that is not a method witness.

method_policy_cases.name: undecodable_did_key_witness_fails_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: The witness id is shaped like a did:key and passes any pattern check, but its multibase payload does not decode to a well-formed public key compatible with the log's Data Integrity cryptosuite. did:webvh 1.0 requires this to be caught during parameter validation, not deferred to signature verification: an undecodable key that is allowed to occupy a threshold slot silently hollows out the threshold, because that slot can never be satisfied by any proof.

method_policy_cases.name: threshold_above_witness_count_fails_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: An unsatisfiable threshold is a declaration error, not an instruction to ignore witnessing.

method_policy_cases.name: duplicate_witness_id_fails_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: A repeated id would let one key be counted twice toward threshold.

method_policy_cases.name: missing_witness_proofs_file_fails_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: Policy is declared but did-witness.json is unreachable or has no entry for this versionId. Unavailable evidence is not absent policy.

method_policy_cases.name: proof_from_unlisted_signer_does_not_count
method_policy_cases.notes: A syntactically fine proof signed by a key outside parameters.witness proves nothing about the declared witness set.

method_policy_cases.name: fewer_valid_proofs_than_threshold_fails_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: One valid proof against a declared threshold of two. Effective threshold is the strictest intersection of the method threshold and the deployment minimum, so a holder can raise this bar but never lower it.

method_policy_cases.name: holder_declared_threshold_cannot_lower_deployment_minimum
method_policy_cases.notes: The log declares threshold 1 while deployment policy requires 2. Effective threshold is 2; otherwise any holder could opt out of the deployment's witnessing requirement by editing its own log.

method_policy_cases.name: same_controlling_organization_does_not_satisfy_distinct_requirement
method_policy_cases.notes: Two distinct witness keys, one operator. Counting keys instead of controlling organizations would let a single operator satisfy a two-organization requirement alone, which empties the requirement of meaning.

method_policy_cases.name: evidence_older_than_max_age_fails_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: Age is measured from observed_at, not from when an Arkret receipt was signed. Re-signing an old observation does not refresh it.

schema_validation_cases.name: did_webvh_witness_receipt_valid
schema_validation_cases.notes: Binds subject DID, exact versionId, witness did:key, its controlling organization and the observation instant. The issuer service DID is the trust root for the receipt itself and is unrelated to the subject DID's controller.

schema_validation_cases.name: registry_consensus_receipt_stays_a_separate_family
schema_validation_cases.notes: The pre-existing family, unchanged. Its witness_role describes a replication role inside a DID registry consensus group and it binds seq + head_event_digest; it says nothing about did:webvh method witnesses. Both families ride ak.root.identity.receipts.read.list.v1 and are told apart only by the schema constant.

schema_validation_cases.name: witness_receipt_without_expiry_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: An Arkret-layer cache record without an expiry is indistinguishable from a permanent assertion, which is exactly how stale witness evidence outlives the state it described.

schema_validation_cases.name: witness_receipt_without_controlling_organization_did_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: Distinct-organization policy counts organizations, not keys. A receipt that cannot name the controlling organization cannot be counted toward that requirement, so the field is required rather than optional.

schema_validation_cases.name: non_did_key_witness_in_receipt_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: witness_did mirrors parameters.witness.witnesses[].id, which did:webvh 1.0 constrains to did:key. A receipt naming another form is describing something that is not a method witness.

schema_validation_cases.name: arkret_overlay_field_on_receipt_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.first_expected_error: $: Additional properties are not allowed ('max_age_seconds' was unexpected)
schema_validation_cases.notes: The receipt records an observation; it does not carry policy. Letting an issuer attach its own max age would put the freshness bar back in the hands of the party whose evidence is being judged.

schema_validation_cases.name: receipts_tagged_union_accepts_both_families
schema_validation_cases.notes: One response carrying both families. A consumer MUST branch on the schema constant; threshold_met is an Arkret-layer convenience and its absence MUST NOT be read as true.
